claims.text: A low-concentration Ni additive introduced during processing will promote transient liquid-phase sintering at W–Cu interfaces.
Adding Ni during processing will form a graded, Ni-enriched interfacial layer between W and Cu.
The graded Ni-enriched layer will chemically and structurally bond the W and Cu phases.
Ni lowers the interfacial energy of the W–Cu interface.
Ni promotes interdiffusion at the W–Cu interface during transient liquid-phase processing.
The Ni-modified interface prevents phase separation during subsequent thermal cycling and irradiation.
The Ni-modified composite will have greater interfacial cohesion than an untreated W–Cu composite.
The Ni-modified composite will have higher thermal conductivity than the untreated composite under comparable heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
Reducing interfacial voids and phase segregation improves heat transfer through the composite.
Untreated W–Cu composites develop phase separation and interfacial voids under the stated thermal and irradiation conditions.
Phase separation and interfacial void formation reduce the thermal conductivity of untreated W–Cu composites.
The intervention is effective only at low Ni concentrations that avoid deleterious secondary phases.
Successful improvement requires a sintering temperature and time that permit transient-liquid formation without over-alloying the composite.
